Problem numbers refer to the textbook (Chiang & Wainwright, 4th edition). These are not graded, but you should attempt them all before the quiz. Try each question yourself first, then expand the **Solution** to check.

## Exercise 7.4

**1.** Find $\partial y / \partial x_{1}$ and $\partial y / \partial x_{2}$ for each of the following functions:

a. $y=2x_{1}^{3}-11x_{1}^{2}x_{2}+3x_{2}^{2}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{\partial y}{\partial x_{1}}=6x_{1}^{2}-22x_{1}x_{2} \qquad \frac{\partial y}{\partial x_{2}}=-11x_{1}^{2}+6x_{2}$$

</details>

d. $y=\dfrac{5x_{1}+3}{x_{2}-2}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial y}{\partial x_{1}} &= \frac{5\left(x_{2}-2\right)-\left(5x_{1}+3\right)\cdot 0}{\left(x_{2}-2\right)^{2}}=\frac{5}{x_{2}-2} \\
\frac{\partial y}{\partial x_{2}} &= \frac{0\cdot\left(x_{2}-2\right)-1\cdot\left(5x_{1}+3\right)}{\left(x_{2}-2\right)^{2}}=\frac{-\left(5x_{1}+3\right)}{\left(x_{2}-2\right)^{2}}
\end{aligned}$$

</details>

**2.** Find $f_{x}$ and $f_{y}$ from the following:

a. $f(x,y)=x^{2}+5xy-y^{3}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$f_{x}=2x+5y \qquad f_{y}=5x-3y^{2}$$

</details>

b. $f(x,y)=\left(x^{2}-3y\right)(x-2)$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\begin{aligned}
f_{x} &= (2x)(x-2)+\left(x^{2}-3y\right)\cdot 1=3x^{2}-4x-3y \\
f_{y} &= -3(x-2)+\left(x^{2}-3y\right)\cdot 0=-3x+6
\end{aligned}$$

</details>

**3.** From the answers to Prob. 2, find $f_{x}(1,2)$, the value of the partial derivative $f_{x}$ when $x=1$ and $y=2$, for each function.

<details class="solution">
<summary>Solution</summary>

For (a), $f_{x}(1,2)=2(1)+5(2)=12$.

For (b), $f_{x}(1,2)=3(1)^{2}-4(1)-3(2)=-7$.

</details>

**5.** If the utility function of an individual takes the form
$$U=U\left(x_{1},x_{2}\right)=\left(x_{1}+2\right)^{2}\left(x_{2}+3\right)^{3}$$
where $U$ is total utility, and $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ are the quantities of two commodities consumed:

a. Find the marginal-utility function of each of the two commodities.

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\begin{aligned}
U_{1} &= \frac{\partial U}{\partial x_{1}}=2\left(x_{1}+2\right)\left(x_{2}+3\right)^{3} \\
U_{2} &= \frac{\partial U}{\partial x_{2}}=3\left(x_{1}+2\right)^{2}\left(x_{2}+3\right)^{2}
\end{aligned}$$

</details>

b. Find the value of the marginal utility of the first commodity when 3 units of each commodity are consumed.

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$U_{1}(3,3)=2(3+2)(3+3)^{3}=2\times 5\times 216=2160$$

</details>

**7.** Write the gradients of the following functions:

a. $f(x,y,z)=x^{2}+y^{3}+z^{4}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$f_{x}=2x \qquad f_{y}=3y^{2} \qquad f_{z}=4z^{3} \qquad \nabla f(x,y,z)=\left[\begin{array}{c}2x \\ 3y^{2} \\ 4z^{3}\end{array}\right]$$

</details>

b. $f(x,y,z)=xyz$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$f_{x}=yz \qquad f_{y}=xz \qquad f_{z}=xy \qquad \nabla f(x,y,z)=\left[\begin{array}{c}yz \\ xz \\ xy\end{array}\right]$$

</details>

## Exercise 8.1

**1.** Find the differential $dy$, given:

a. $y=-x\left(x^{2}+3\right)$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

Since $y=-x^{3}-3x$, $$dy=\left(-3x^{2}-3\right)dx=-3\left(x^{2}+1\right)dx$$

</details>

**4.** Find the point elasticity of demand, given $Q=k/P^{n}$, where $k$ and $n$ are positive constants.

a. Does the elasticity depend on the price in this case?

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

Writing $Q=kP^{-n}$, $\dfrac{dQ}{dP}=-nkP^{-n-1}$, so

$$\varepsilon_{d}=\frac{dQ}{dP}\cdot\frac{P}{Q}=\frac{-nkP^{-n-1}\cdot P}{kP^{-n}}=-n$$

No: the elasticity is the constant $-n$, whatever the price.

</details>

b. In the special case where $n=1$, what is the shape of the demand curve? What is the point elasticity of demand?

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

With $n=1$, $Q=k/P$, so $PQ=k$: the demand curve is a rectangular hyperbola, downward sloping and approaching both axes. The point elasticity is $\varepsilon_{d}=-1$ everywhere (unit elastic).

</details>

**6.** Given $Q=100-2P+0.02Y$, where $Q$ is quantity demanded, $P$ is price, and $Y$ is income, and given $P=20$ and $Y=5{,}000$, find the

a. Price elasticity of demand.

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

At $P=20$ and $Y=5{,}000$, $Q=100-40+100=160$, so

$$\varepsilon_{P}=\frac{\partial Q}{\partial P}\cdot\frac{P}{Q}=-2\cdot\frac{20}{160}=-0.25$$

</details>

b. Income elasticity of demand.

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\varepsilon_{Y}=\frac{\partial Q}{\partial Y}\cdot\frac{Y}{Q}=0.02\cdot\frac{5000}{160}=0.625$$

</details>

## Exercise 8.2

**3.** Find the total differential, given

a. $y=\dfrac{x_{1}}{x_{1}+x_{2}}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{\partial y}{\partial x_{1}}=\frac{1\cdot\left(x_{1}+x_{2}\right)-x_{1}\cdot 1}{\left(x_{1}+x_{2}\right)^{2}}=\frac{x_{2}}{\left(x_{1}+x_{2}\right)^{2}}$$

$$\frac{\partial y}{\partial x_{2}}=\frac{-x_{1}}{\left(x_{1}+x_{2}\right)^{2}}$$

$$dy=\frac{x_{2}\,dx_{1}-x_{1}\,dx_{2}}{\left(x_{1}+x_{2}\right)^{2}}$$

</details>

**4.** The supply function of a certain commodity is
$$Q=a+bP^{2}+R^{1/2} \quad (a<0,\ b>0) \quad [R\text{: rainfall}]$$
Find the price elasticity of supply $\varepsilon_{QP}$, and the rainfall elasticity of supply $\varepsilon_{QR}$.

<details class="solution">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\varepsilon_{QP}=\frac{\partial Q}{\partial P}\cdot\frac{P}{Q}=\frac{2bP\cdot P}{Q}=\frac{2bP^{2}}{a+bP^{2}+R^{1/2}}$$

$$\varepsilon_{QR}=\frac{\partial Q}{\partial R}\cdot\frac{R}{Q}=\frac{1}{2}R^{-1/2}\cdot\frac{R}{Q}=\frac{R^{1/2}}{2\left(a+bP^{2}+R^{1/2}\right)}$$

</details>

**5.** How do the two partial elasticities in Prob. 4 vary with $P$ and $R$? In a strictly monotonic fashion (assuming positive $P$ and $R$)?

<details class="solution">
<summary>Solution</summary>

Write $Q=a+bP^{2}+R^{1/2}$ and assume $Q>0$. For $\varepsilon_{QP}=2bP^{2}/Q$:

$$\frac{\partial \varepsilon_{QP}}{\partial P}=\frac{4bP\,Q-2bP^{2}\cdot 2bP}{Q^{2}}=\frac{4bP\left(a+R^{1/2}\right)}{Q^{2}}$$

$$\frac{\partial \varepsilon_{QP}}{\partial R}=\frac{-bP^{2}R^{-1/2}}{Q^{2}}<0$$

So $\varepsilon_{QP}$ is strictly decreasing in $R$. In $P$ it is strictly increasing if $a+R^{1/2}>0$ and strictly decreasing if $a+R^{1/2}<0$: the sign does not depend on $P$, so it is strictly monotonic in $P$ either way.

For $\varepsilon_{QR}=R^{1/2}/(2Q)$:

$$\frac{\partial \varepsilon_{QR}}{\partial P}=\frac{-bP\,R^{1/2}}{Q^{2}}<0$$

$$\frac{\partial \varepsilon_{QR}}{\partial R}=\frac{R^{-1/2}\,Q-1}{4Q^{2}}=\frac{R^{-1/2}\left(a+bP^{2}\right)}{4Q^{2}}$$

So $\varepsilon_{QR}$ is strictly decreasing in $P$. In $R$ it is strictly increasing if $a+bP^{2}>0$ and strictly decreasing if $a+bP^{2}<0$: again the sign does not depend on $R$, so it is strictly monotonic in $R$.

</details>

**6.** The foreign demand for our exports $X$ depends on the foreign income $Y_{f}$ and our price level $P$: $X=Y_{f}^{1/2}+P^{-2}$. Find the partial elasticity of foreign demand for our exports with respect to our price level.

<details class="solution">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\varepsilon_{XP}=\frac{\partial X}{\partial P}\cdot\frac{P}{X}=\frac{-2P^{-3}\cdot P}{Y_{f}^{1/2}+P^{-2}}=\frac{-2}{Y_{f}^{1/2}P^{2}+1}<0$$

</details>

**7.** Find the total differential for each of the following functions:

b. $U=7x^{2}y^{3}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\begin{aligned}
dU &= U_{x}\,dx+U_{y}\,dy \\
&= 14xy^{3}\,dx+21x^{2}y^{2}\,dy \\
&= 7xy^{2}\left(2y\,dx+3x\,dy\right)
\end{aligned}$$

</details>

f. $U=(x-3y)^{3}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\begin{aligned}
dU &= 3(x-3y)^{2}\,dx+3(x-3y)^{2}(-3)\,dy \\
&= 3(x-3y)^{2}\left(dx-3\,dy\right)
\end{aligned}$$

</details>

## Exercise 8.4

**2.** Find the total derivative $dz/dt$, given

a. $z=x^{2}-8xy-y^{3}$, where $x=3t$ and $y=1-t$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{dz}{dt} &= z_{x}\frac{dx}{dt}+z_{y}\frac{dy}{dt} \\
&= (2x-8y)(3)+\left(-8x-3y^{2}\right)(-1) \\
&= 14x-24y+3y^{2} \\
&= 42t-24(1-t)+3(1-t)^{2}=3t^{2}+60t-21
\end{aligned}$$

</details>

b. $z=7u+vt$, where $u=2t^{2}$ and $v=t+1$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{dz}{dt} &= z_{u}\frac{du}{dt}+z_{v}\frac{dv}{dt}+z_{t} \\
&= 7(4t)+t\cdot 1+v \\
&= 28t+t+t+1=30t+1
\end{aligned}$$

</details>

c. $z=f(x,y,t)$, where $x=a+bt$ and $y=c+kt$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{dz}{dt}=f_{x}\frac{dx}{dt}+f_{y}\frac{dy}{dt}+f_{t}=bf_{x}+kf_{y}+f_{t}$$

</details>

**4.** Find the partial total derivatives $\S W/\S u$ and $\S W/\S v$ if

a. $W=ax^{2}+bxy+cu$, where $x=\alpha u+\beta v$ and $y=\gamma u$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{\S W}{\S u} &= W_{x}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}+W_{y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}+W_{u} \\
&= (2ax+by)\alpha+bx\gamma+c \\
&= (2a\alpha+b\gamma)(\alpha u+\beta v)+\alpha b\gamma u+c
\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{\S W}{\S v} &= W_{x}\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}+W_{y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial v} \\
&= (2ax+by)\beta+bx\cdot 0 \\
&= \beta\left[(2a\alpha+b\gamma)u+2a\beta v\right]
\end{aligned}$$

</details>

b. $W=f\left(x_{1},x_{2}\right)$, where $x_{1}=5u^{2}+3v$ and $x_{2}=u-4v^{3}$

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

$$\frac{\S W}{\S u}=f_{1}\frac{\partial x_{1}}{\partial u}+f_{2}\frac{\partial x_{2}}{\partial u}=10u\,f_{1}+f_{2}$$

$$\frac{\S W}{\S v}=f_{1}\frac{\partial x_{1}}{\partial v}+f_{2}\frac{\partial x_{2}}{\partial v}=3f_{1}-12v^{2}f_{2}$$

</details>
